text: 4 This is a method to make an n by n magic square where n is odd.
Step 1 Place the smallest integer in the middle square of the top row.
Step 2 Move up and right in the direction of the left diagonal to place the next integer.
Different 3 by 3 magic squares are made using the first nine terms of a sequence.
The first term of the sequence is 2.
The nth term of the sequence is 3n - 1.
Find six of these magic squares.
Use the method of Question 4 and reflection to help you.
When n is even there is no middle square so we use a different method to make a magic square.
• Draw the two diagonals on the 4 by 4 square.
• Put the smallest integer in the top left square.
• Go from left to right, but only write the integers in the squares where there is part of a diagonal.
• Starting with the bottom row write the remaining integers, in order, from right to left in the empty
squares.

B MODELLING (QUESTIONS 8 to 10)
DELIVERIES BY SCOOTER (30 marks)
You are advised to spend no more than 50 minutes on this part.
This task looks at average speeds of deliveries made by scooter.
A company delivers orders from its warehouses to shops and houses.
All deliveries of small parcels are made by scooter.
8 (a) Meera rides a scooter that travels 12 km in 15 minutes on quiet roads.
Show that her average speed on quiet roads is 48 km/h.
